entry.evidence: This study examines whether individual faults of the Carson Range fault system (CRFS) rupture randomly through time, cluster temporally, or rupture together as large multifault [...]

steps.action: Poses the question of whether the faults of the Carson Range fault system rupture randomly, cluster in time, or rupture together, motivated by the scarcity of known clusters.
steps.quote: This study examines whether individual faults of the Carson Range fault system (CRFS) rupture randomly through time, cluster temporally

steps.action: States three rival rupture behaviours: random (time-independent) rupture, temporal clustering (supercycle), and large multifault ruptures.
steps.quote: rupture randomly through time, cluster temporally, or rupture together as large multifault [...]

steps.action: Measures scarp vertical separation from lidar topographic profiles along the whole fault system and plots VS below 10 m against northward distance.
steps.quote: Figure 3a shows the locations of vertical separation (VS) measurements along the CRFS

steps.action: Omits scarps on an older glacial outwash terrace and compares the resulting bell-shaped offset distribution with rangefront topography and published slip rates.
steps.quote: consistent with not only topography, where the highest displacements are situated along the steepest sections of rangefront

steps.action: Attributes the smallest offsets to the most recent event and larger ones to multiple events, draws a hand-fit slip-per-event reconstruction, and interprets the slip pattern as distributed slip on the northern splays.
steps.quote: I propose one possible slip-per-event reconstruction (gray lines) created using a visual fit

steps.action: Collates event horizons and radiocarbon ages from about a dozen prior trenching studies along the system and surrounding faults.
steps.quote: the event horizons from prior trenching studies along the CRFS and surrounding faults were first collated

steps.action: Recalibrates the ages in OxCal to build stratigraphic models that bracket event windows at each trench, rejecting two ages as the original investigators did.
steps.quote: their results were recalibrated using OxCal (Bronk Ramsey, 1995) to produce stratigraphic models bracketing event windows

steps.action: Sets a correlation rule: overlapping windows on adjacent segments form one event, and an ambiguous window is grouped with the younger neighbour.
steps.quote: considered singular events if the event timing overlaps and the fault segments are adjacent

steps.action: Derives an event model of five surface-rupturing events (E1-E5) with rupture lengths, displacements, timing, and Mw6.4-7.3 magnitudes.
steps.quote: results in an event model with five independent surface rupturing events across the CRFS

steps.action: Compares the event model with lidar scarp character and with the vertical separation distribution.
steps.quote: model is consistent with geomorphic observations bearing both on the recency and continuity of fault scarp character

steps.action: Considers the alternative that E2 is the same event as E1 (requiring rejection of two fissure ages) and states that the outcome does not change significantly.
steps.quote: It is possible that E2 is actually E1, as interpreted by the original authors

steps.action: Keeps the interpretation of non-persistent rupture boundaries: E1 stopped at the Kings Canyon-Jacks Valley earthquake gate, while E4 crossed it.
steps.quote: provides an example of a fault system with non-persistent segment/rupture boundaries

steps.action: Sets the segmentation variability beside a similar published result for the Wasatch fault.
steps.quote: DuRoss et al. (2016) found a similar variability of past rupture segmentation for the Wasatch fault in Utah.

steps.action: Adds two published ruptures of nearby faults (East Carson Valley and Incline Village) within the last millennium to the event set.
steps.quote: [...] ruptures of nearby faults have also been shown to have occurred during the last millennium.

steps.action: Argues against random rupture because individual fault recurrence times are 3 to 30 times the 300-year span of the cluster.
steps.quote: suggesting this is a non-random process, and represents a period of increased seismicity

steps.action: Checks the cluster against nearby reference faults (West Tahoe, Polaris, Antelope Valley, Smith Valley) that did not rupture during the cluster window.
steps.quote: Other nearby faults did not rupture during this time

steps.action: Compares the Carson Range cluster with historical normal-fault clusters in the Apennines and the Central Nevada Seismic Belt (Figure 5).
steps.quote: Similar earthquake clusters in normal faulting environments have been observed before in both the Apennines

steps.action: Concludes that at least five surface-rupturing earthquakes between about 800 and 500 cal ybp form a spatiotemporal cluster, with implications for seismic hazard.
steps.quote: surface rupturing earthquakes in the Walker Lane have been spatially and temporally clustered in the past

end.claim: At least five Mw6.4-7.3 surface-rupturing earthquakes occurred near Carson City within about 300 years (about 800-500 cal ybp), forming a spatiotemporal earthquake cluster or supercycle.

decisive_move.sentence: Recalibrating the collated trench ages in OxCal and correlating event windows across adjacent segments into a five-event model is what produces the cluster; without it the scarp data alone allow many interpretations.

gates.evidence: All trench data are reanalysed from prior studies and the lidar was pre-existing, so no hypothesis directed acquisition (p. 4, 8). Non-randomness rests on a qualitative contrast between recurrence intervals and cluster duration (p. 7), with no statistical test against a Poisson null. The event correlation rule is stated but not shown to have been fixed before the ages were seen (p. 6).

imports.item: OxCal Bayesian radiocarbon calibration and stratigraphic modelling
Airborne lidar topography (USGS Reno-Carson QL1/QL2, Douglas County)
Cumulative structural damage from successive earthquakes

limits: Inference: the event model rests on a correlation rule (adjacency plus overlap, ties grouped with the younger window) whose alternatives are not run, except for the E2 reinterpretation. The non-random claim is not tested statistically against a Poisson model. The slip-per-event reconstruction is a hand-drawn visual fit. The consistency check with lidar geomorphology uses data that also informed the reconstruction, so it is not an independent test (coded as C, not V). The author states that timing resolution cannot separate simultaneous multifault ruptures from sequences lasting minutes to centuries (p. 6), so the multifault rival is not excluded. Sub-claims: E1 timing (515-421 cal ybp), length (about 60 km), and Mw about 7 are estimate_with_resolution (p. 7-8); non-persistent rupture boundaries are best_explanation (p. 7). Inclusion of the ECV and IVF events in the cluster relies entirely on cited studies. No review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.target: Pierce, Wesnousky, Saha, & Moon (2021), interpretation of the Indian Hills event as the same event as E1
disagreements.support: The OxCal recalibration places the Indian Hills rupture as a separate event E2 (1,265-591 cal ybp); merging it with E1 would require rejecting two fissure-deposit ages.
disagreements.quote: It is possible that E2 is actually E1, as interpreted by the original authors (Pierce, Wesnousky, Saha, & Moon, 2021)

disagreements.target: Poisson or time-independent rupture models underpinning most PSHA (e.g., Field et al., 2014)
disagreements.support: A reconstructed 300-year cluster on faults with recurrence 3-30 times longer implies time-dependent, elevated hazard after recent seismicity.
disagreements.quote: as opposed to the poisson or time-independent rupture models that underpin most probabilistic seismic hazard assessment (PSHA) models

disagreements.support: E1 and E4 terminate at different points and rupture different combinations of segments.
disagreements.quote: This result suggests that it might be difficult to predict the endpoints of future ruptures

alternatives_considered.reason: Paleoseismic data are mostly limited to the two most recent earthquakes, which together produced less than 10 m of slip

alternatives_considered.chosen: Omit scarps on the about 20 ka glacial outwash terrace near the 10 km mark
alternatives_considered.reason: The surface is at least about 15 ka older than most late Holocene surfaces

alternatives_considered.chosen: Combine the scarp data with trench event timing
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Slip-per-event reconstruction from displacement data alone (many possible interpretations)
alternatives_considered.reason: Displacement data alone lead to many possible interpretations

Treat overlapping windows on adjacent segments as single events
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Separate earthquakes on neighbouring faults over minutes to centuries
alternatives_considered.reason: Event timing constraints are not of sufficient resolution to differentiate

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Group it with the older window
alternatives_considered.reason: Post-event limiting ages come from colluvium assumed to be deposited rapidly after an earthquake

alternatives_considered.alternatives: E2 equals E1, as interpreted by the original authors
